slides.kicker: The Intent Signal Playbook, in 9 slides
slides.title: You don't have a lead problem. You have a timing problem.
slides.sub: 412 accounts in the saved view. A rule for finding the 40 worth calling this week.

slides.title: Static lists bury the accounts that are ready.

tiles.label: accounts in the view, all technically in the ICP, sorted by company name
worth a call this week. Nothing in the view says which.

slides.after: The company quietly evaluating three vendors sits at row 287, indistinguishable from row 286. Buying more contacts adds rows to the same pile.

slides.title: One signal is close to worthless. Independence is the whole trick.

rows.label: Weak
rows.note: Someone read your blog. One family.

rows.label: Better
rows.note: They came back for the product page. Still one family.

rows.label: Strong
rows.note: Category research off-site, product page on-site, a competitor searched. Two families.

rows.label: Very strong
rows.note: Three families that could not have caused each other.

slides.after: Four families to combine: first-party, third-party, business triggers, and the relationships already in your CRM.

slides.title: Six dimensions, weighted to 100, scored in ninety seconds.

rows.label: Fit
rows.note: Do they look like a company that buys this? Weight x5.

rows.label: Intent
rows.note: What do they appear to be researching? x4.

rows.label: Recency
rows.note: How fresh is the behaviour? x3.

rows.label: Engagement
rows.note: Are they interacting with us specifically? x3.

rows.label: Trigger
rows.note: What changed inside the company? x3.

rows.label: Buyer relevance
rows.note: Are the right roles involved? x2.

slides.after: Fit is heaviest because it is the only dimension that does not decay.

slides.title: A six-week-old signal describes a moment that has passed.
slides.after: Recency score by days since the newest signal. Tune the windows to your cycle: a six-month cycle can stretch "very recent" to 21 days.

slides.title: Three tiers and one exit ramp.

cards.title: Tier 1. Contact now
cards.text: Same-day outreach, one written hypothesis. 15 to 25 accounts per SDR per week, never more.

cards.title: Tier 2. Research and monitor
cards.text: Named owner, weekly review. Promote the moment a second signal family fires.

cards.title: Tier 3. Nurture
cards.text: Marketing's, not an SDR's. Be credible when the trigger eventually happens.

cards.title: Disqualify
cards.text: Remove it and record why. High intent never overrides poor fit.

slides.title: Five minutes, five questions, one written hypothesis.

items.label: Minute 1
items.text: **Fit.** Name the closest existing customer and the use case.

items.label: Minute 2
items.text: **Intent.** What problem is in play, in the buyer's words?

items.label: Minute 3
items.text: **Recency.** When, and is it a cluster or a single point?

items.label: Minute 4
items.text: **Trigger.** What changed in the last 90 days that you can reference?

items.label: Minute 5
items.text: **Buyer.** Who owns this problem? A person, not a title.

visuals.text: Because **[observable change]**, and given **[area of interest]**, **[role]** may be working on **[specific problem]**.

slides.title: Use intent to pick the account. Never to write the message.

items.text: "Hey Dana, I noticed your company has been researching sales engagement software. Do you have 15 minutes Thursday?"
"Dana, you've added nine SDRs since July. Teams usually start looking at how outbound is managed when hiring outpaces the managers who can coach it. Is that the shape of the problem on your side?"

slides.after: The test: would the sentence still make sense if the signal data had never existed?

slides.title: 100 accounts down to 5, in one week.
